newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Feb weekly award pay rates unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Australia Feb weekly award pay rates unchanged.

text.p: Australian weekly award pay rates index for full-time adult employees was unchanged at 147.1 in February from the previous month, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said on Monday.
The February index was 1.3 percent higher than the same month in 1996.

Major increases over the 12 months were in the transport and storage industry, which increased to 143.0 from 139.8, and the recreation, personal and other services industry, up 3.3 points to 153.9, the bureau said.
The index for full-time women workers increased 1.6 percent over the year to 150.1 from 147.8, compared with a 1.2 percent increase for full-time working men, to 145.7 from 144.0.
The index, which covers a minority of workers, measures pay rates set under labour contracts agreed between unions and employers, called awards. Its base is June, 1985.
These increases lag well behind other wage measures.
Average weekly ordinary time earnings increased 1.2 percent in the three months to November, 1996, for annual growth of 3.9 percent, according to bureau figures released in February.
February Industrial Relations Department data on national enterprise bargaining deals showed agreements struck in the December quarter increased an average annualised 4.4 percent.
